newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller cleared of second graft charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller cleared of second graft charge.

text.p: A parliamentary commission on Thursday rejected a second bid to send Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, to the Supreme Court on corruption charges stemming from her time as head of government.

"Sending Mrs Ciller to the Supreme Court over TOFAS has been rejected after a vote," commission chairman Hayrettin Uzun told reporters. A commission on Monday rejected another corruption charge against Ciller.

Ciller had been facing allegations that she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies during her time as prime minister from 1993 until earlier this year. The TOFAS allegations constituted the more serious of three charges she faced.
The commission voted 10 to four with one abstention against sending Ciller to the court for personally interfering in the sale and eight to seven against a second count of abuse of office.
The commission recommended that MPs vote within the next two weeks against sending Ciller, Turkey's first woman leader, to the highest court in the land.

Ciller, a pro-Western secularist, in June joined a coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan -- something she vowed she would never do until the corruption allegations emerged earlier this year.

Political analysts say Ciller, who relies on Erbakan's backing to avoid trial on suspicion of graft, would be freer to oppose Erbakan from within the government if all the charges were dropped. She may even go as far as breaking up the coalition, analysts say.

Ciller was cleared on Monday of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company in her time as prime minister from 1993 until earlier this year. Another commission will rule in the coming weeks on investigations into Ciller's substantial wealth.
